pages.note: Both render the humoral-causation refutation correctly, keep the opponent's 'gtan tshigs ma grub' objection (lines 3-4) and the 'ma grub pa ma yin te' reply separate, and correctly mark the phlegm objection that runs into the next page (lines 6-7, 'gal te bad kan... zhe na').

Both translate the two prayogas (lamp/water, rice sprout/water) and the semen-not-fixed-to-one-woman argument correctly. B's gloss of ཁྱབ་པར་བྱེད་པ་འགལ་བ་དམིགས་པ as 'contradiction in the pervasion' is looser than A's 'contradictory pervader' but does not change the argument.

B_serious.english: Indeed, it changes; however, if form and the other senses are also branches, then ... desire would necessarily arise. This is because form ... act as co-operative causes. If one objects to this, it is not so, because there is certainty for all.
B_serious.problem: The 'zhe na' that closes the opponent's form-as-auxiliary-cause objection is attached to the reply, giving 'If one objects to this, it is not so'. Read that way, the reply seems to defend the form argument rather than reject it, and the objection is presented as the author's own statement.

pages.note: The image's first syllable may read ཕྱིར་ where the OCR has ནི་, which does not matter for meaning. Both handle the impurity-meditation prayoga correctly, but B blurs who is speaking in the opening objection and reply, while A marks it cleanly.
